Install Claude Science on macOS, Windows, or Linux, sign in with your Claude account, and run your first analysis.
Claude Science in its own window on macOS
Keep working when Claude Science switches to its own window on a Mac: open, quit, and update it, and turn macOS permissions back on.
Install the latest version of Claude Science on Mac, Windows, or Linux, and get past an Update required message or an update that fails.
A project groups related sessions and the artifacts they produce.
Auto mode lets Claude Science run code and call connectors without stopping to ask about every step.
Use Claude Science on more than one computer
What to expect when you sign in on another computer, or under another sign-in on the same computer.
Artifacts in Claude Science are files Claude saves into a project, such as figures, datasets, and reports. Open, version, trace, and delete them.
Comments in Claude Science pin a note to a specific part of an artifact, such as selected text or a point on a figure, and send the note to Claude.
A built-in verification step that independently re-reads Claude's recent responses, the approved plan, saved artifacts, and the execution record, then checks whether its claims match what ran.
Run on a remote Linux server
Install Claude Science on a cloud VM or lab server and use it from your own browser through an SSH tunnel.
Claude writes and runs Python, R, and shell commands.
Connectors give Claude access to external data sources during an analysis.
Connect a machine you can reach over SSH (a lab workstation or an HPC login node) so Claude can run jobs on it.
Claude Science can run jobs on an external cloud provider you control, and connect to model servers that serve scientific models over HTTP.
Connect Amazon S3, Google Cloud Storage, or Azure Blob Storage so Claude can read data and write results in place, with your permission.
Claude retrieves open-access full text without credentials; add publisher keys or a library proxy to reach paywalled text you're entitled to.
Add any Model Context Protocol (MCP) server as a Remote (HTTPS web server) or Local command (program on your computer).
Browse nine example prompts from nine fields of science, each the start of a complete analysis in Claude Science.
Genetic drift in a bottle: Buri's 107 fruit-fly populations
Simulate 107 bottles of 16 fruit flies drifting by chance alone and compare them with Peter Buri's real bottles (1956).
A titration curve from the full equilibrium: which indicator finds the equivalence point?
Solve the full equilibrium for 25.0 mL of 0.100 M acetic acid as 0.100 M NaOH is added, without the usual shortcuts.
A first Kaplan–Meier curve: the 1963 leukemia trial of 6-MP
Compare 6-MP against placebo with Kaplan–Meier curves from 42 remission times typed into the prompt.
PageRank on a web of 11 pages: why 1 good link beats 6 weak ones
Follow a random surfer on Wikipedia's 11-page example until the numbers settle, and reproduce all 11 published values to 0.1 point.
A first finite-element model: a clamped steel ruler bends and vibrates
Split a 300 mm steel ruler clamped at one end into 4 beam elements and check its bending under 1 N and its first 3 vibration modes against beam theory.
A first X-ray diffraction pattern: why silicon shows 6 peaks and salt 9
Simulate the X-ray powder patterns of silicon and table salt and label every peak with Bragg's law.
The Ulam spiral: are the primes' diagonal streaks real?
Compare the share of primes per diagonal on Ulam's 1963 spiral of 1 to 40,401 against as many random odd numbers.
The double slit, one electron at a time
Rebuild the picture of Tonomura's 1989 experiment with an ideal double slit: each electron lands as 1 random dot, yet fringes 10.7 µm apart build up.
Schelling's segregation model: ask for 30% same-color neighbors, end up with 75%
Ask for 30% same-color neighbors, end up with about 75%: the textbook computer version of Thomas Schelling's 1971 idea.
What happens when a model's safeguards flag a message, how to switch models automatically, and how to choose a use case under the Life Sciences Verification Program (beta).
Fix errors you see while using Claude Science: being signed out, capacity retries, Agent Failed, environment setup, connectors, git, dictation, and updates.
One-sentence definitions for the terms you meet in Claude Science, from artifact to workspace.
Reference for the claude-science command: its subcommands, the serve flags, the single-use login link, and the environment variables you can set.
Claude Science's config.toml file: where it lives, how it interacts with Settings, and its network, web search, and upload keys.
Release notes for Claude Science, including new features, improvements, and bug fixes by version.
Legal agreements, compliance certifications, and security information for Claude Science.
Claude Science is a desktop app for scientific research.
How Claude Science works with your data

What Claude Science keeps on your computers, what it sends to Anthropic and how long Anthropic keeps it, who can access it, Anthropic's no-training and ownership commitments, and the controls available to your organization.

Claude Science is a desktop application that stores member content locally.
Use Claude Science on a corporate network
How to run Claude Science behind an outbound proxy, a TLS-inspecting proxy, an internal package mirror, and an egress firewall, with the settings your network team needs for each.

The domains Claude Science connects to, grouped for a proxy or firewall allowlist: the app's connections to Anthropic, the analysis sandbox's package and research domains, the domains a package mirror adds and removes, and the built-in list of domains it always blocks.

provenance.basis: Human0's claude_domain.csv (sha256 d26d41d8da4ed7dd622b6e6faa18a97dc91d4f3d2af972ae9715d41ee94963cc), converted by tools/claude_domain/build_claude_packs.py on 2026-11-27. Topics, concepts, skills (docs pages) and agent names are Human0's. A single-page skill's description is that page's own one-line description where the site publishes one (page_descriptions.json: llms.txt / llms-full.txt fetched 2026-11-27); concept descriptions, other skill descriptions, keywords, skill types (a verb rule), ids and the lexicon are generated from the CSV text.
provenance.mcp_notes: Human0's CSV lists 'Claude Developer Platform docs' for this topic, but that server (Claude Platform Docs, directory cc6f3470-080c-45b8-84e1-cdc03e9c6ac1) covers platform.claude.com only, by its own instructions, and a search for 'Claude Code hooks' on 2026-11-27 returned only platform.claude.com pages. No MCP server for these docs was verified, so the pack lists none.
provenance.limitations: Skills without a published page description (API reference endpoints and some guides) are described by their titles only; skill types come from the first word of the title. Docs pages change: the URLs were current in the CSV, not re-checked here.
